docs.title: seqforge
docs.text:
seqforge reads public sequencing studies and their files, and writes down what they are, so that each dataset can be processed the right way. It does two jobs.

  • It reads a study. Given a GEO Series, it works out which records and papers make up the study (the study's bounds). Then it works out what each sample was: the factors the study varied on purpose, each sample's level of each, and labels such as species, tissue and assay (the study's reading).
  • It compiles a dataset. Given FASTQ files, it works out from the bytes which sequencing technology made them and which file holds what. Then it writes a pipeline that you submit to a cluster.

One report shows a study's bounds and reading, a compiled dataset, or both, on one web page. See three example reports before you read on.

The two halves run on their own. A study can be read without compiling any of its files, and a dataset can be compiled with no study at all. They meet in the sample table: when you compile with --study, each sample's row takes the reading's factors and labels, matched by its BioSample accession (the archive's id for the biological sample). The manifest does not change.

docs.title: Why you can trust it
docs.text:
• A model answers only where code can check the answer. In a reading, every claim quotes a passage that code finds again, word for word, in the record or paper. A claim with no such passage is marked inferred.
  • Each question is asked twice. The second time, the options come in reverse order. If the two answers differ, the study is marked unsettled, so you know which answers to check.
  • The bytes decide the technology. A paper that names a kit is a hint. The reads in the files decide, and when the two disagree, seqforge stops and says so.
  • It refuses rather than guesses. A refusal is an exit code with a reason and a suggested fix, not a best guess.
  • It never reads a whole FASTQ file. A small, fixed head of each file is enough.
  • Every study file and manifest is checked against its written format before it is saved.

Why you can trust the output explains each point.

docs.title: Where it stands
docs.text: The study chain is built and run on the standard set, 50 GEO studies picked to cover many designs. Most of them settle, and a first run costs a few cents a study in model calls. The dated note on the latest run gives the counts and the cost. Nothing on this site scores those readings against a person's answers: measuring accuracy is a separate effort.

docs.title: What it does not do
docs.text:
• It does not submit jobs. You run the Snakefile on your own cluster.
  • It does not judge its own accuracy.
  • Reading a study needs the lab's model gateway and its copy of the GEO and SRA records. Compiling calls the gateway only to read prose, such as a paper or the archive's records, and seqforge run --no-llm skips that step.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
seqforge does two jobs, and you can use either one alone:

  • Read a set of studies. You give it a list of GEO Series (GEO is the Gene Expression Omnibus, the public archive of sequencing studies). For each study it writes which Series and papers belong to it, and what each sample was.
  • Compile a dataset. You give it FASTQ files (the raw reads off a sequencer) and any notes or papers about them. It writes down what the data is and gives you a pipeline that turns the reads into count tables.

This page installs seqforge, checks that it works, and says what each job needs.

docs.title: Install it
docs.text:
seqforge needs Python 3.13 or newer. Pick one of the two ways to install it.

Inside the lab, from a clone. pixi is the tool that builds the lab's software environments. It also installs the two lab packages that seqforge reads from: liulab-genome (genomes and their annotation files) and liulab-data (the lab's local copy of archive records, papers and ontologies).

git clone https://github.com/liuhlab/seqforge
cd seqforge
pixi install

In the clone, put pixi run in front of each command on this site, or run pixi shell once to open a shell that has seqforge on its path.

Anywhere, from PyPI. PyPI is the public index of Python packages.

pip install seqforge

That gives you the seqforge command. Reading studies and compiling against a real genome also need the two lab packages, which are not on PyPI:

pip install "liulab-genome @ git+https://github.com/liuhlab/liulab-genome.git" \
            "liulab-data   @ git+https://github.com/liuhlab/liulab-data.git"

docs.title: Check that it works
docs.text:
These three commands need no network, no model and no data of your own.

seqforge version
seqforge kb list
seqforge kb roundtrip 10x-3p-gex-v3

seqforge version prints the version number. seqforge kb list prints one line for each sequencing technology seqforge knows, such as 10x-3p-gex-v3 and smartseq3. seqforge kb roundtrip makes fake reads for one technology, reads them back, and prints JSON that lists each check it ran. Look for "passed": true near the top.

docs.title: Let Claude run it (optional)
docs.text:
seqforge ships skills for Claude Code, an AI assistant that runs in your terminal. A skill tells Claude which seqforge commands to run for a task. To install them for your user, run this in the clone:

pixi run install-skills

Then you can ask Claude in plain words, for example "read the studies in this folder" or "compile the FASTQ files in ./data".

docs.title: What each job needs
docs.text:
Job What goes in What it needs Read studies A list of GEO Series The lab's model gateway, and liulab-data with its record store, paper store and ontology store Compile a dataset FASTQ files, and optionally an accession and a paper The model gateway only to read a paper or notes. liulab-genome for the genome. A cluster to run the pipeline

Here is what each of those is.

  • The lab's model gateway is the lab's server for language models. seqforge sends every model question through it, so you need no account with a model provider. Open a tunnel to it and set $LABLLM_GATEWAY to the tunnel's local address. Reach the lab gateway says how.
  • The record store is liulab-data's local copy of GEO and SRA records (SRA is the Sequence Read Archive, where the reads themselves are kept). $LABDATA_STORE points at it. The paper store ($LABDATA_PAPERS) holds the papers, and the ontology store ($LABDATA_ONTOLOGIES) holds the term lists that a reading names each tissue, cell type and condition from.
  • A cluster is a shared computer with many processors. The compiled pipeline runs the aligner there. seqforge writes the pipeline but never starts it: you submit it.

docs.title: Read a set of studies
docs.text:
One command reads a folder of studies under a spending limit in dollars:

seqforge study run --studies <folder> --ceiling-usd 2

A first run costs a few cents a study. The guide Read your own studies sets up the folder, explains the three ways a study can end, and makes a report for each study. To see the output first, open the example reports.

docs.title: Compile a dataset
docs.text:
One command takes FASTQ files to a pipeline:

seqforge run reads/*.fastq.gz --accession PRJNA1027859 --doc paper.pdf \
    --assembly ce11 --annotation WS298

The genome is the one choice you must make. --assembly names it by its UCSC id (the assembly's name in the UCSC Genome Browser), and --annotation names the gene annotation file registered for it. The accession and the paper are optional, and --no-llm skips the model, so nothing reaches the gateway.

seqforge writes everything under seqforge/ in the current folder. seqforge/manifest.yaml records what the data is. The pipeline is a Snakefile under seqforge/pipeline/, which you submit to the cluster with Snakemake (a tool that runs a pipeline step by step). Add --study <folder>/<ID> to copy a study's reading into the sample table.

Two tutorials walk the whole path:

  • Compile with Claude: describe your data and let Claude run the commands.
  • Compile step by step: run each command yourself and look at what it wrote.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Most commands print one JSON object, and every command reports its result through its exit code, so a script can act on the code alone. 0 means it worked. 3 and 4 are seqforge refusing to guess: 3 means blocked or stopped, and 4 means a person must decide. Commands lists every code, and every command with what it needs.

docs.title: Files from the hand work
docs.text: This page lists every file in the standard set's folder. It is for someone outside the project who builds an evaluation on these files. For each kind of file, it gives the path, the count, the format, who made the file and how, and a few lines of Python that load it.

docs.title: Five words this page uses
docs.text:
• A study is one piece of research: the experiments one paper reports, or one project that has no paper yet.
  • A Series is one deposit in GEO, the Gene Expression Omnibus, a public archive of sequencing data. A Series has an id such as GSE241718. One study can span several Series.
  • A study's bounds say which Series and which papers belong to the study.
  • The standard set is a fixed list of 50 small GEO studies.
  • A study's reading says what each sequenced sample is and which labels the study varied.

Hand work means work done one study at a time, outside the unattended chain that the study workflow describes. The name does not mean that a person did it. A model made every file on this page, or code wrote the file from a model's answer. No person has checked any of them.

docs.title: Every file in one table
docs.text:
All files are under evals/standard-set/ in the seqforge repository. <ID> is the Series that a study was picked by. It is also the name of the study's folder. The counts were measured on 2026-11-27.

File Path Count Made by Format The pick pick.yaml 1 A model session, 2026-11-19 On this page The study file <ID>/study.yaml 50 The judge command On this page The bounds <ID>/bounds.yaml 50 Code, from the two models' answers The bounds file The job's bounds <ID>/job-bounds.yaml 50 The bounding job, typesafe/jev-1.14.0, 2026-11-27 The bounds file The job's reading <ID>/job-reading.yaml 50 The reading job, deepseek/deepseek-flash and typesafe/jev-1.14.0, 2026-11-27 The reading file The draft <ID>/draft.yaml 50 deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash On this page The verdict <ID>/verdict.yaml 50 claude-fable-5-2 On this page The reading <ID>/reading.yaml 5 claude-fable-5-2 The reading file The reading's verdict <ID>/reading.verdict.yaml 5 claude-fable-5-2, in a second pass On this page The reading's notes <ID>/reading.notes.md 5 The model that wrote the reading Markdown text A person's answers none yet 0 Nobody yet The rule

That is 316 files: the pick, six files for each of the 50 studies, and three more for each of the five studies that have a worked reading. The folder also holds a README.md, which describes the commands.

This snippet counts the files again. Run it, and every other snippet on this page, from the root of the repository. Each snippet needs Python 3 and PyYAML and nothing else.

import collections
import pathlib

root = pathlib.Path("evals/standard-set")
print(len([p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()]))  # 50
print(sorted(collections.Counter(p.name for p in root.glob("*/*")).items()))

The files hold identifiers and the models' own words. They hold two kinds of text copied from a record or a paper:

  • short quotes, most of them under passages in a reading;
  • titles, in the titles map of each job-bounds.yaml.

The records are public at GEO, and PubMed lists each paper by its number.

docs.title: The jobs' files
docs.text:
The two jobs of the study workflow wrote one file each in every study folder. They sit beside the set's own bounds.yaml and reading.yaml, under other names, so neither job writes over the set's own files.

All 100 files were deleted and written again on 2026-11-27, by one run of both jobs over the 50 studies. The run used seqforge at commit 9209509, the bounding job's version 2026.11.3, and the reading job's version 2026.11.10. The note on that run gives its cost and how each study ended. No study's ending and no claim moved since the run of 2026-11-26.

A file does not say how its study ended: settled, unsettled or refused. That is kept in the pass's task, and the note lists it.

docs.title: job-bounds.yaml: the bounding job's bounds
docs.text:
Path: evals/standard-set/<ID>/job-bounds.yaml. 50 files.

Format: The bounds file describes every field. All 50 files say format: 1.

Made by: the bounding job. A pass of seqforge pass start study-bounds answered each study, and this command wrote the files:

seqforge study write-bounds --out evals/standard-set --name job-bounds.yaml

models names typesafe/jev-1.14.0 in 46 files. In the other 4 it is null, because the study's linked group held no record for Jev to place: GSE112068, GSE142633, GSE208154 and GSE240375.

What these files hold that the set's own bounds do not:

  • A probability. Each claim that Jev answered has a p, and its text gives Jev's two answers. A claim that code made, such as the starting Series, has p: null.
  • titles, new on 2026-11-27. It maps each record the bounds place, kept or left out, to its title, copied from the Series record or the paper. A record with no title has no entry.
import yaml

with open("evals/standard-set/GSE241718/job-bounds.yaml", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    bounds = yaml.safe_load(handle)
print(bounds["models"], [(claim["id"], claim["p"]) for claim in bounds["series"]])
print(bounds["titles"])

docs.title: job-reading.yaml: the reading job's reading
docs.text:
Path: evals/standard-set/<ID>/job-reading.yaml. 50 files.

Format: The reading file describes every field. All 50 files say format: 2.

Made by: the reading job, from each study's own bounds.yaml. A pass of seqforge pass start study-reading answered each study, and this command wrote the files:

seqforge study write-reading --out evals/standard-set --name job-reading.yaml

models.reading is deepseek/deepseek-flash, and models.probabilities is typesafe/jev-1.14.0.

The run was on the evening of 2026-11-27 in Boston, but each file's ontology_snapshot.date says 2026-11-28. That date is the day in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) when the pass opened the ontology store, because the store names its snapshots by UTC day.

What these files hold that they did not before:

  • biosample_accession, new on 2026-11-27. A sample's row carries it when the sample's GEO record links exactly one BioSample. It is the BioSample's SAMN id, copied from the record. It is an id, not a claim. 785 of the 787 rows carry one. The two rows without one are in GSE254687.
import yaml

with open("evals/standard-set/GSE241718/job-reading.yaml", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    reading = yaml.safe_load(handle)
print(reading["ontology_snapshot"])
for sample, row in reading["samples"].items():
    print(sample, row.get("biosample_accession"))

docs.title: The standard set
docs.text:
The 50 studies were picked on 2026-11-19. A small model then drafted each study's bounds, and a large model judged each draft once. Three commands did that work, and all three are now retired:

  1. A pass of the standard-set-bounds kind asked the small model about each study.
  2. The standard-set draft command wrote draft.yaml from the answers.
  3. The standard-set judge command asked the large model about one study. It wrote verdict.yaml, bounds.yaml and study.yaml.

The bounding job now draws a study: the study workflow says how. You can load every file here without liulab-data, the lab's package that stores the GEO records and the papers.

The judge agreed with 48 drafts and replaced 2, those of GSE101112 and GSE126954. It was unsure about none.

docs.title: pick.yaml: the 50 picked, the spares and the replaced
docs.text:
Path: evals/standard-set/pick.yaml. One file.

Made by: a model session on 2026-11-19. The file names no model, and its first line marks it PROVISIONAL. Its header says that the picker judged each study's direction, shape and design from the Series' public GEO record and the PubMed abstract of its paper. The picker read 302 Series records and 263 abstracts, a count taken from the note on record links.

The file has six top-level fields:

Field Holds store_build The build of liulab-data's store that the counts and the links were read from: 20261107T163933Z. picked_on The date of the pick: 2026-11-19. limits The size limits a study had to fit: the most samples, experiments and linked Series, and the fewest sequenced runs (min_sequenced_runs). The hard_shape_ limits are wider and apply to a study picked for a hard shape. studies The 50 picked studies: 17 on aging, 17 on neurodegeneration and 16 on C. elegans. spares 14 studies held back to take the place of a picked study that fails. replaced The studies taken out after the pick, each with the spare that took its place and the reason it failed. The list is empty: no study has been replaced.

Each entry of studies and of spares has these fields:

Field Holds id The Series the study was picked by. direction aging, neurodegeneration or c_elegans. A study counts under one. also_fits The other directions the study could count under. May be empty. hard_shape The hard case the study was picked for: recites_older_series, paper_over_several_series, superseries, series_with_two_studies or series_without_paper. null for a plain study. 34 of the 50 are null. linked_series Every Series linked to the picked one, the picked one included. pmids Every paper linked to any of those Series, each a PubMed number written as text. assay The kind of sequencing, in the picker's short words. compiles_today The library chemistry that the record's protocol text points to, by the name seqforge gives it. A list when the study has two, and null when seqforge supports none. No sequencing read was looked at. compiles_fully true when every library of the study is in a chemistry that compiles_today names. known_dataset true for a study that seqforge had already worked on before the pick. 5 of the 50. n_samples, n_experiments The GEO samples and the SRA experiments of all the linked Series together. SRA is the Sequence Read Archive, which holds the reads. design The design, in the picker's short words. reason_picked One or two sentences. status settled, shape_to_confirm or shape_not_found. The last one marks a study picked as possibly two studies in one Series that turned out to be one study. 3 of the 50. spare_for Spares only. The direction or the hard shape that the spare stands in for. 
import yaml

with open("evals/standard-set/pick.yaml", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    pick = yaml.safe_load(handle)
print(len(pick["studies"]), len(pick["spares"]), len(pick["replaced"]))  # 50 14 0
print(pick["studies"][0]["id"], pick["studies"][0]["reason_picked"])

docs.title: study.yaml: the facts about one pick
docs.text:
Path: evals/standard-set/<ID>/study.yaml. 50 files.

Made by: the retired standard-set judge command, when it wrote the verdict. It copies the pick's facts, takes summary from the draft, and adds three fields from the verdict. Each file was rewritten once, on 2026-11-20 (UTC), to move the bounds out into bounds.yaml.

Field Holds id The folder name: the Series the study was picked by. summary One short line that says what the study is. From the draft. direction, also_fits, hard_shape, reason_picked As in pick.yaml. store_build The store build the identifiers were read from. All 50 files say 20261107T163933Z-subset. The subset is a small copy of the build that pick.yaml names, cut down to the records of these studies. records Every linked record, by identifier only: series, superseries (which of those Series is a SuperSeries, or null), bioprojects and pmids. bounds_from draft when the judge agreed with the draft (48 files), judge when the judge's bounds replaced it (2 files). status settled, or unsure when the judge was unsure. All 50 say settled. read_to_decide What the judge had to read: records, abstract, full_paper. 
import yaml

with open("evals/standard-set/GSE241718/study.yaml", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    study = yaml.safe_load(handle)
print(study["id"], study["direction"], study["records"]["series"], study["bounds_from"])

docs.title: bounds.yaml: the study's bounds
docs.text:
Path: evals/standard-set/<ID>/bounds.yaml. 50 files.

Format: The bounds file describes every field. All 50 files say format: 1.

Made by: code, which converted the bounds that the two models drew. models.bounds names the model whose bounds became the study's: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash in 48 files and claude-fable-5-2 in 2. The files hold no date. Git history dates the conversion to 2026-11-20 (UTC).

The 50 files hold 74 claims: 57 Series kept and 17 records left out, in 10 studies. Seven studies have two Series. Four studies have no paper. In three studies the folder's Series is a SuperSeries, so it is in left_out and not in series: GSE117724, GSE140511 and GSE240375.

import pathlib

import yaml

for path in sorted(pathlib.Path("evals/standard-set").glob("*/bounds.yaml")):
    bounds = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    kept = [claim["id"] for claim in bounds["series"]]
    left_out = [claim["id"] for claim in bounds["left_out"]]
    print(bounds["study"], kept, bounds["papers"], left_out)

docs.title: draft.yaml: what the small model answered
docs.text:
Path: evals/standard-set/<ID>/draft.yaml. 50 files.

Made by: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, through the drafting pass and the draft command. The model read the records of the linked Series and the abstract of each paper, and nothing else. The drafts are dated from 2026-11-19 23:38 to 2026-11-20 00:05 (UTC).

Field Holds id The study. model The model that answered. pass The pass that asked: its kind, its version and its number, such as standard-set-bounds/2026.11.3/pass-5. The 50 drafts come from four passes. when The time of the answer, as text: 2026-11-20T00:02:16Z. summary One line that says what the study is. bounds The model's answer. See below. checks_failed What the code found malformed in the answer. Empty in 49 drafts. The draft of GSE126954 put a sample id among the left-out records.

bounds in a draft is the model's answer. It is not in the bounds format:

Field Holds series The Series the model kept. papers The papers the model kept, each written pmid:<number>. reason One line. left_out A mapping from each record left out to the reason. In bounds.yaml the same thing is a list of claims. split_samples An older field. See What this page promises. 
import yaml

with open("evals/standard-set/GSE241718/draft.yaml", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    draft = yaml.safe_load(handle)
print(draft["model"], draft["pass"], draft["when"])
print(draft["bounds"]["series"], draft["bounds"]["papers"], draft["bounds"]["left_out"])

docs.title: verdict.yaml: what the judge answered
docs.text:
Path: evals/standard-set/<ID>/verdict.yaml. 50 files.

Made by: claude-fable-5-2, through the judge command, once for each study. The judge got the draft and what the drafting model saw. It could also open the full records and the full text of the papers. The verdicts are dated from 2026-11-19 23:38 to 2026-11-20 00:10 (UTC).

Field Holds id The study. model The model that judged. when The time of the verdict, as text. agrees true when the judge agrees with the draft's bounds. 48 are true and 2 are false. bounds null when the judge agrees. Otherwise the judge's own bounds, with the same five fields as the bounds in a draft. reason Why the judge agrees or disagrees. unsure true when the judge could not decide. All 50 are false. read What the judge read: records, abstract, full_paper. The judge opened a full paper for 7 studies.

The bounds that the two models settled on are the draft's when the judge agrees, and the judge's when it does not:

import pathlib

import yaml

for folder in sorted(pathlib.Path("evals/standard-set").glob("GSE*")):
    draft = yaml.safe_load((folder / "draft.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    verdict = yaml.safe_load((folder / "verdict.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    answer = draft["bounds"] if verdict["agrees"] else verdict["bounds"]
    print(verdict["id"], verdict["agrees"], answer["series"], sorted(answer["left_out"]))

docs.title: The five worked readings
docs.text:
Five of the 50 studies have a reading of their own, one for each kind of design. A model wrote each reading. A second model pass checked each reading against the records and the paper. No person has checked any of them. Where the second pass disagrees with a reading, the reading is left as written, and the disagreement is in the verdict.

Study Kind of design Samples Passages Second pass agrees Disagreements GSE100021 Two groups: a treatment against a control 8 29 No 1 GSE112068 A dose series and a time series 23 45 No 3 GSE235532 Pull-down libraries with their input controls 24 30 Yes 1 GSE117724 Two assays: 18 RNA-Seq libraries and 2 ChIP-Seq libraries 20 54 Yes 0 GSE241718 One paper over two Series 8 28 Yes 2

No command made these files. The process was:

  1. A large model read the records of the study's Series and its paper. It wrote reading.yaml and reading.notes.md. For four studies it read the records, the abstract and the full text. GSE112068 has no paper, so the model read the records only.
  2. A second pass read the same sources again and checked the reading. It looked for every quote in the field or the paper section that the reading names. It compared the samples with the study's bounds. It wrote reading.verdict.yaml.
  3. The second pass changed a reading only to make it pass the format check. Each such change is listed under format_fixes in the verdict: 7 changes over the five readings.

Each file records the model as claude-fable-5-2, for the reading, for its probabilities and for the second pass.

docs.title: reading.yaml: the study reading
docs.text:
Path: evals/standard-set/<ID>/reading.yaml. 5 files.

Format: The reading file describes every field. All five files say format: 2. They were written in format 1 and rewritten to format 2 on 2026-11-21. That change added the assay's ontology id, the source of the ids, and the passages that speak against a claim. No claim's text, number, level or p changed. Each reading.notes.md ends with what changed in it.

Made by: claude-fable-5-2, named in models.reading and in models.probabilities. The files do not say when they were written. They were added to the repository on 2026-11-20 (UTC). Their ontology_snapshot.date is 2026-11-21, the day of the rewrite to format 2.

These five files carry no biosample_accession on any row. The job's job-reading.yaml beside each one does.

A sample has every claim under shared, except a label that its own row writes. The snippet applies that rule:

import yaml

with open("evals/standard-set/GSE241718/reading.yaml", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    reading = yaml.safe_load(handle)
for sample, row in reading["samples"].items():
    claims = {**reading["shared"], **row}  # a row's claim replaces the shared claim whole
    print(sample, claims["tissue"]["text"], claims["age"]["level"], claims["assay"]["p"])
print(reading["passages"][14]["quote"])  # a passage number loads as a whole number

The relations between the samples are not stored. seqforge study relations <file> works them out, and the reading file describes its output.

docs.title: reading.verdict.yaml: what the second pass found
docs.text:
Path: evals/standard-set/<ID>/reading.verdict.yaml. 5 files.

Made by: claude-fable-5-2, in a second pass. The verdicts are dated from 2026-11-20 01:39 to 02:05 (UTC).

Field Holds id The study. model The model of the second pass. when The time of the verdict. Four files write it as text. GSE100021/reading.verdict.yaml writes it without quotes, so PyYAML returns a datetime for that one file. read What the second pass read: records, abstract, full_text. format_fixes A list of text. Each item is one change that the second pass made to reading.yaml so that the file passes the format check. quotes Three counts of the quotes in the reading: checked, found, and not_found, a list. In all five, every quote was found: 186 quotes together. samples_match_bounds true when the samples of the reading are exactly the samples of the Series in the study's bounds. true in all five. agrees The second pass's overall judgement of the reading. true in 3 and false in 2. A verdict can agree and still list disagreements. disagreements A list, one item for each point where the second pass would write the reading differently. May be empty. unsure A list of text: what the second pass could not settle from the sources. Each verdict has 3 to 6. reason The second pass's account of what it checked and found.

Each item of disagreements has five fields:

Field Holds where The place in reading.yaml, such as shared.dose or samples.GSM7720368.donor. One item can name several places. says What the reading says there. should_be What the second pass would write. why The reason. passages The passages that the point rests on, by number. One item in the verdict of GSE241718 also quotes a record line as text. 
import pathlib

import yaml

for path in sorted(pathlib.Path("evals/standard-set").glob("*/reading.verdict.yaml")):
    verdict = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    print(verdict["id"], verdict["agrees"], verdict["quotes"]["found"], len(verdict["unsure"]))
    for item in verdict["disagreements"]:
        print("  ", item["where"], "->", item["should_be"])

docs.title: reading.notes.md: what the format could not hold
docs.text:
Path: evals/standard-set/<ID>/reading.notes.md. 5 files.

Made by: the model that wrote the reading, at the same time. Each file is free Markdown text with no fixed fields. It says what the model read. It also says what the reading format could not hold for this study, or held badly.

import pathlib

for path in sorted(pathlib.Path("evals/standard-set").glob("*/reading.notes.md")):
    notes = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    print(path.parent.name, notes.splitlines()[0])

docs.title: Answers a person gave while checking
docs.text:
There are none yet. No person has answered a question about any of the 50 studies, and no person has corrected a file. Every study folder holds only the files in the table at the top.

The rule for the first one is fixed. An answer that a person gives while checking is saved as a small plain file. The file holds the question, the study, the answer, who gave it and when. No folder and no command exist for such files yet. When the first answer is saved, this page lists its path.

docs.title: What this page promises
docs.text:
Every file listed here is at the listed path, in the current format. There is one format at a time. A change to a format rewrites every existing file in the same change, and this page changes with it. The page does not promise that the content of a file stays the same.

Two kinds of file have a written format and a check:

seqforge study check-bounds evals/standard-set/<ID>/bounds.yaml
seqforge study check-reading evals/standard-set/<ID>/reading.yaml

The reading check needs liulab-data installed, because liulab-data's vocabularies judge each ontology id. On 2026-11-27, every file that has a check passed it: the 50 bounds.yaml, the 50 job-bounds.yaml, the five reading.yaml and the 50 job-reading.yaml.

The other files have no format number, and their fields are the ones this page lists. The drafts and the verdicts are kept as the models wrote them, so they hold fields from before the bounds format:

  • split_samples is in the bounds of all 50 drafts, and in the bounds of the 2 verdicts that have bounds of their own. It comes from when one Series could be split between two studies. A study is now whole Series, and the bounds format rejects the field. It is empty in all 50 drafts and in the verdict of GSE101112. In the verdict of GSE126954 it lists seven sample ids.
  • left_out in a draft or a verdict is a mapping from a record to a reason. In bounds.yaml it is a list of claims.
  • A paper is written pmid:<number> in the bounds, the drafts, the verdicts and the readings. In pick.yaml and in study.yaml it is the bare number, as text.
  • A full paper is full_paper in study.yaml and verdict.yaml, and full_text in the two reading files.

docs.title: Known wrong or stale facts in the files
docs.text:
Do not build on these lines without reading this list. Each one was checked against the files on 2026-11-27.

  1. GSE241718/study.yaml describes the two Series wrongly. Its reason_picked says that one Series holds whole cells and one holds nuclei. The protocol on every sample record, the summary of both Series and the paper say that all eight libraries are single-nucleus. The paper says that the data were uploaded in two stages. The entry in pick.yaml has the same sentence, and its assay and design say the same. That entry also names the chemistry as 10x-3p-gex, while the protocol on every sample record names a Singleron kit.
  2. GSE126954/bounds.yaml still speaks of seven samples. Its claim and its reason say that "the seven embryo samples are its own data". The judge had drawn the study as seven of the eight samples. A study is whole Series, so the bounds are now the whole Series of eight. The eighth sample is a re-deposited sample of an older study. Telling it apart is left to the study's reading. The set has no worked reading of this study. The job's job-reading.yaml reads all eight samples, and no one has checked it.
  3. The set's own bounds carry no probability and no quote. All 74 claims in the 50 bounds.yaml files are marked inferred, with the model's reason as the text. Every p is null, models.probabilities is null, and passages is empty. null means that no model has given a probability, not that the claim is in doubt. The job's job-bounds.yaml files do carry a p on each claim that Jev answered.
  4. One when is later than its file. GSE100021/reading.verdict.yaml says 2026-11-20T02:05:00Z. The commit that added the file is dated 23 minutes earlier. The model wrote the time itself.
  5. The readings keep what the second pass disagrees with. The table below has one line for each reading.
Reading What the second pass disagrees with GSE100021 shared.dose writes the value 1.7e+12 with the unit viral_particles_per_side. The source sentence gives the content of the suspension, not the amount each side received. GSE112068 shared.sex is na and should be unknown, on all 23 samples. The three untreated samples have control as their treatment, where na fits. The time factor cites passages that do not list its levels. GSE117724 Nothing. The second pass lists four points it could not settle, such as the stage of the worms at harvest. GSE235532 The reading leaves out the time of collection, and its notes say wrongly that the format has no place for it. GSE241718 The donor ids of the four young libraries are a guess, and their p of 0.5 is too high. Passage 19 names two sample records, and all eight hold the quote.

The second pass also could not settle the age of the four aged libraries of GSE241718. The sample records say 24 months, and the Series designs and the paper say 26. The reading writes 26 with a p of 0.55.

docs.title: Passes
docs.text:
Some of seqforge's work asks a language model the same kind of question once for each of many studies. seqforge runs that work as a pass. A pass takes one kind of work and a list of units, each named by a key such as a GEO Series id. It asks the models about each unit, and it records how each unit ended. A pass never spends more than the dollar ceiling you give it.

The engine behind a pass is the lab package liulab-llms. It sends every model call through the lab gateway, the one server that holds the lab's model keys. It caches every answer, stops at the ceiling, and keeps its record in a task folder. seqforge names its kinds and starts their passes. The engine's own words are defined in liulab-llms's glossary.

seqforge has two kinds. Both work on a folder of study folders.

Kind What one unit does Models it uses study-bounds Draws one study's bounds: which GEO Series and papers belong to it. See bound the study. jev: typesafe/jev-1.14.0 study-reading Reads what each sequenced sample of one study is. See read the study. writer: deepseek/deepseek-flash, thinking on; jev: typesafe/jev-1.14.0

Jev is a model that answers yes-or-no and multiple-choice questions with a probability. A model's role is the name a kind gives to each model it asks, such as writer or jev; it is the name before the = in --model.

docs.title: What a pass needs
docs.text:
Every pass needs the lab gateway, and the two study kinds also read the lab's stores of archive records, papers and ontologies. Each store is part of liulab-data, the lab's data package. Set these variables before you start a pass:

Variable What it points to Which kinds need it $LABLLM_GATEWAY The lab gateway's local address, such as http://127.0.0.1:8000, served by a tunnel you open Both LABDATA_STORE liulab-data's store of GEO and other archive records Both LABDATA_PAPERS liulab-data's paper store: each paper's abstract, and its full text where the store holds one Both, for any study that links a paper LABDATA_ONTOLOGIES liulab-data's ontology store, the vocabularies that a reading's ids come from study-reading

Reach the lab gateway shows how to open the tunnel. Each liulab-data store can also be found through a pointer that liulab-data saves for you, in place of its variable.

A kind opens each store once, when the pass starts. The whole pass reads that one build of the record store and those ontology snapshots, even if a store is refreshed while the pass runs.

docs.title: Start a pass
docs.text:
seqforge pass start <kind> --ceiling-usd <dollars>

This command calls the gateway and reads the stores above. With no --keys, a study kind runs the studies that the folder's pick.yaml lists, in that order. The folder is the standard set, evals/standard-set, unless --studies names another.

The options:

Option What it does --ceiling-usd The most the pass may spend, in dollars. Required: it has no default. --model ROLE=PROVIDER/NAME[,KEY=VALUE...] The model for one role, such as writer=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash,thinking=off. Repeat it for more roles. The keys are thinking (on or off), effort, temperature and max-output-tokens. --keys FILE Run exactly these units, one key per line, in this order. A key listed twice is refused. --studies DIR The folder of study folders that the pass works on. Default: evals/standard-set. --only ENDINGS Run only the units whose current ending is one of these, comma-separated, such as unsettled,refused. You cannot give both --keys and --only. --units-at-once How many units run at once. Default: 32. --off-peak-only Send calls only outside the model's peak hours. A call made in peak hours waits for them to end. --label The pass's name in the gateway's record. Default: the kind's name. --task DIR The task folder. Default: seqforge/passes/<kind>/ in the current folder.

A role that you do not name with --model takes the kind's default model. A role that you do name takes exactly what you write: a setting you leave out takes liulab-llms's default, not the kind's. The gateway has no short names for models, so NAME is the provider's exact model name.

docs.title: How a unit ends
docs.text:
Each unit ends in one of five ways:

Ending What it means settled The answer passed every check. unsettled The answer failed a check. A person or a stronger model should look at it. refused The kind's code declined to answer the unit, and said why. unfinished The pass stopped, or the unit's code failed, before the unit ended. held An input that the unit needs is missing, such as the study's bounds file.

What makes a study settled, unsettled, refused or held is the kind's own rule. The study workflow gives each kind's rules.

docs.title: The ceiling
docs.text: The ceiling is a dollar amount for this one pass. Before each model call, the engine checks whether the call's largest possible cost would cross the ceiling. If it would, the pass stops with ceiling_reached and exits 3. An answer replayed from the gateway's cache costs nothing. A ceiling must be a number of dollars, zero or more.

docs.title: What a pass prints
docs.text:
While the pass runs, it writes progress lines to stderr:

  • one line as it starts: the kind, how many units, the ceiling, how many at once, and the task;
  • a line at most every 30 seconds: the units ended so far, by ending, the dollars spent, and the time taken;
  • one line as it ends: whether it reached the end of its units or stopped and why, the counts, the dollars spent, the requests sent, and the answers from the cache.

stdout carries one JSON object and nothing else:

Field Value kind, kind_version The kind, and its version. The version is set by hand and changes when a question or a rule of the kind changes. task The task folder. pass_id, label The pass's number in the task, and its label. store_build The build of liulab-data's record store that the pass read, or null for a kind that reads no record store. models Each role's full model. keys How many units the pass was given. counts How many units ended each way: settled, unsettled, refused, unfinished and held, zeros included. stopped, message Why the pass stopped, and the gateway's message about it. Both are null when the pass reached its end. spent_usd What the pass paid. first_cost_usd What its answers cost when each was first paid, answers from the cache included. requests, cache_hits Requests sent to providers, and answers that came from the cache.

stopped is one of these:

stopped Why ceiling_reached The next call could cross the ceiling. provider_exhausted The provider's prepaid balance or monthly cap is used up. provider_unavailable The provider still failed after the gateway's retries. gateway_unreachable The gateway could not be reached. task_in_use Another process holds the task. message names it: who, which process, on which machine, and since when.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Exit When 0 The pass reached the end of its units, whatever the counts. 2 A setup the pass cannot use. One line on stderr says which. 3 The pass stopped: one of the reasons in the stopped table.

A setup that exits 2 is one of these:

  • an unknown kind;
  • a store the kind reads that cannot be opened;
  • a role the kind does not have, or a role with no model;
  • a model text or a keys file it cannot read, or a key listed twice;
  • both --keys and --only, or an ending --only does not know;
  • no --keys for a folder that has no pick.yaml;
  • no gateway address, or a ceiling that is not a number of dollars;
  • a model name the gateway rejects;
  • a task folder that this version of liulab-llms cannot read.

docs.title: Resume a pass
docs.text:
Run the same command again. There is no resume option. Every unit answered before comes back from the gateway's cache at no cost, and cache_hits counts them. After a stop at the ceiling, raise --ceiling-usd and run the command again.

Run it from the same folder, or give the same --task, so that the pass finds its task.

docs.title: See where a kind stands
docs.text:
seqforge pass status <kind>

This command reads the kind's task and prints one JSON object. It sends nothing to the gateway and opens none of the stores, so it works with the gateway down. It takes no hold on the task, so it also works while a pass runs. It takes --task DIR as pass start does.

Field Value kind, task The kind, and the task folder. units How many units any pass of the kind has recorded. counts Each unit's current ending: settled, unsettled, refused or dropped, a person's review included. Then the units whose latest outcome is unfinished or held. A unit settled once and unfinished in a later pass counts under both. not_done Each unit whose latest outcome is unfinished or held, in key order: its key, that ending, the outcome's reason, and the pass it came from. passes Every pass of the kind, oldest first.

dropped is an ending only a person's review gives. not_done lists every such unit, with no cap. A held study's reason says what it lacks, such as its bounds file. To see only the held units, filter the list with jq, a tool that reads JSON:

seqforge pass status study-reading | jq '.not_done[] | select(.ending == "held")'

A refused or unsettled unit is not in not_done. study write-bounds and study write-reading list each of those, with each refused study's reason. Unlike pass status, they refuse to run while a pass holds the task: they exit 3 with stopped: task_in_use.

Each item of passes gives the same fields as pass start prints for its pass: pass_id, label, kind_version, models, store_build, counts, stopped, spent_usd, first_cost_usd, requests and cache_hits. It also gives:

  • ceiling_usd, the pass's ceiling;
  • ended, which is false for a pass that was killed before it ended;
  • per_unit, the cost and time per unit.

per_unit covers the units that called a model in that pass. An answer from the cache counts. A held unit, or one the pass never started, does not. units says how many there were. For each of spent_usd, first_cost_usd, requests and seconds, it gives the total, the median and the 90th percentile (p90).

Exit When 0 The report is on stdout. 2 An unknown kind, a folder that holds no task, or a task that a pass stopped in the middle of a write. One line on stderr says which. 3 A pass's write kept the read waiting, and message says so. Run the command again.

A task that a pass stopped in the middle of a write is fixed by the next pass start of the kind. That pass also runs every unit not yet answered, so it can spend up to its --ceiling-usd.

docs.title: Send the hard units to a stronger model
docs.text:
After a pass, you can run only the units that did not settle, on a stronger model. Name the role and the model with --model:

seqforge pass start <kind> --ceiling-usd <dollars> --only unsettled,refused --model writer=<provider>/<name>

This needs the gateway and the stores, as any pass does.

A unit that a person's review holds counts with the review's ending, as long as its inputs have not changed since the review. So --only unsettled leaves out a unit that a person has settled. liulab-llms reads a task's reviews from the reviews/ folder inside the task folder. No seqforge command writes there. The folder holds only the reviews saved with liulab-llms's own Reviews.save, and a task with no such folder has no reviews.

docs.title: The study workflow
docs.text:
This page gives each step of the study chain in order, and the rules each step follows.

What goes in: one GEO Series id per study. GEO, the Gene Expression Omnibus, is a public archive of sequencing data, and a Series is one deposit in it, with an id such as GSE100021. The chain reads the Series' archive records and the papers they link. It never reads sequencing data.

What comes out: two files in each study's folder.

  • bounds.yaml holds the study's bounds: the Series and the papers that belong to it, and each linked record that was left out, with the reason.
  • reading.yaml holds the study reading: what each sequenced sample was, which labels the study varied on purpose, and the quotes that back each statement.

Why you can check it: models answer, and code decides whether an answer stands. Code finds every quote again in its source. Each question that decides an ending is asked twice, in two forms, and the two answers must agree. Every file passes its format check before it is written.

docs.title: Words this page uses
docs.text:
• A study is one piece of research: the experiments one paper reports, or one project that has no paper yet. A study is whole Series. No step splits a Series by sample.
  • A study folder holds one study's files. It is named by the Series the study starts from, such as GSE100021.
  • A folder of study folders holds many study folders. Its pick.yaml lists the studies to run. A folder with no pick.yaml needs a --keys file that names them, one Series per line.
  • The standard set is a fixed list of 50 small GEO studies in evals/standard-set/. The chain is built and checked on it, and it is the folder a pass uses when --studies names none.
  • Jev is a model that answers yes-or-no and multiple-choice questions with a probability.
  • A job is one step that models do for each study: bounding or reading. Each job runs as a pass, a run of one kind of work over many studies under a dollar ceiling.

docs.title: The steps in order
docs.text:
# Step Command Needs Writes 1 Bound the study seqforge pass start study-bounds, then seqforge study write-bounds The gateway, the record store and the paper store bounds.yaml 2 Check the bounds seqforge study check-bounds <file> Nothing No file. It prints whether the file is valid 3 Read the study seqforge pass start study-reading, then seqforge study write-reading The gateway and the record, paper and ontology stores reading.yaml 4 Check the reading seqforge study check-reading <file> liulab-data installed No file. It prints whether the file is valid 5 Work out the relations seqforge study relations <file> liulab-data installed No file. It prints the relations 6 Run the chain unattended seqforge study run --studies <folder> --ceiling-usd <dollars> As steps 1 and 3 bounds.yaml and reading.yaml for each study

The gateway is the lab's model server, reached at $LABLLM_GATEWAY. The stores belong to liulab-data, the lab's data package: the record store (LABDATA_STORE), the paper store (LABDATA_PAPERS) and the ontology store (LABDATA_ONTOLOGIES). Passes says how to set each one.

Steps 1 to 5 handle one study at a time. Step 6 runs steps 1 and 3 over every study of a folder.

docs.title: Rules that every step follows
docs.text:
One format at a time. Every bounds.yaml and every reading.yaml starts with the line format: <number>. Each check accepts only the current number, and its message names the number it expected. A change to a format rewrites every existing file in the same change, so no file stays in an older format.

A file is never overwritten. write-bounds and write-reading write a study's file only when none is there. To take a newer answer, delete the old file by hand and write again.

A file that fails its check is not written. Each write runs the format check on the exact text it would write.

A person never blocks a step. No step waits for a person's answer. A study the chain cannot settle keeps its best answer, with each probability, or it is listed with the reason it stopped. If a person does answer a question while checking, the answer is saved as a small plain file: the question, the study, the answer, who gave it and when.

No step reads sequencing data. Every step works from archive records and papers.

docs.title: 1. Bound the study
docs.text:
Bounding draws one study out of its linked records. One GEO Series can link to other Series and to papers that belong to a different study, such as an older dataset that the study re-uses. The bounding job decides which linked records belong.

seqforge pass start study-bounds --ceiling-usd 0.1 --studies <folder>
seqforge study write-bounds --out <folder>

The first command needs the gateway, the record store and the paper store. The second reads only the pass's task. Give both commands the same folder. With no --keys, the pass runs the studies that the folder's pick.yaml lists.

docs.title: What the bounding job reads
docs.text:
For each study, the job gathers the linked group: the starting Series, every Series one link away from it, and every paper that those Series link. Four kinds of link count:

  • a SuperSeries and its sub-Series (a SuperSeries is a Series that groups other Series);
  • a shared BioProject, the archive's record of one research project;
  • two BioProjects under one umbrella BioProject;
  • a shared paper.

A reanalysis link counts for nothing, and so does a paper that only a BioProject links. Jev reads each Series record with its samples, and each paper's title, journal, date, publication type and abstract. It never reads a full paper.

docs.title: How the bounding job decides
docs.text:
1. Code keeps the starting Series. When the study starts from a SuperSeries, code keeps each of its sub-Series instead. Code leaves every SuperSeries out, because a SuperSeries only repeats its sub-Series' samples.
  2. Jev is asked about each other Series and each paper, twice: once as written, and once reversed. For a Series, the question is whether it was deposited for the same research. For a paper, the question is whether it is the paper that first reports the data. A preprint and its journal version both count.
  3. An answer is yes when Jev's probability of yes is above 0.5, and no when it is below 0.5. At exactly 0.5 it is neither.
  4. A record is in the study when Jev's answer to the question as written is yes. The two answers agree when one is yes and the other is no.

Each claim in the file is inferred. A claim that code made says so, and has no probability. A claim that Jev made gives Jev's probability of yes to both questions, and carries p. A kept paper is listed by its id only. Its two answers are kept in the pass's task, because the file has no place for them.

The job also copies each placed record's title into the file's titles map, from the Series record or the paper. That covers every record kept or left out. A record with no title has no entry.

docs.title: How the bounding job ends a study
docs.text:
seqforge study write-bounds --out <folder> writes each study's answer as <folder>/<ID>/bounds.yaml, or under the name that --name gives. For the standard set, the job's file is job-bounds.yaml, beside the set's own bounds.yaml. While a pass holds the task, the write refuses and writes nothing: it exits 3 with stopped: task_in_use and names the process that holds the task. Run it again once the pass ends.

Ending When File Settled Jev's two answers agree on every record Written Unsettled Jev's two answers do not agree on a record Written, with each probability Refused The group holds more than 50 Series, Jev gives no answer about a record, or the bounds fail the format check None. write-bounds prints the reason, such as group too large: <n> Series Held The key is not a GEO Series, the record store does not hold the starting Series, or the study links a paper and no paper store is set None. seqforge pass status study-bounds lists the study under not_done

docs.title: How the standard set got its bounds
docs.text:
The 50 studies of the standard set got their own bounds.yaml before the bounding job was built, from commands that are now retired. A small model drafted each study's bounds in a pass of the standard-set-bounds kind. The standard-set draft command wrote each answer as <ID>/draft.yaml. The standard-set judge command asked a large model about one draft, and wrote <ID>/verdict.yaml, <ID>/bounds.yaml and <ID>/study.yaml.

seqforge standard-set list is the one command left. It prints one JSON object per study, from its study file and its bounds file. Files from the hand work says what each file holds.

docs.title: 2. Check the bounds
docs.text:
seqforge study check-bounds <folder>/<ID>/bounds.yaml

The check reads one bounds file and nothing else. It opens no store and calls no model. It prints one JSON object: the file, the format number it accepts, whether the file is valid, and each problem, naming the field and the reason.

Exit When 0 The file is valid. 3 The file is rejected. 2 The file cannot be read.

The check asks only whether the file is in the current format. It does not judge whether the bounds are right. The reader reads each study's bounds file through the same check. A study whose file is missing or rejected is held, and its reason names each problem.

docs.title: 3. Read the study
docs.text:
The reader writes one study's study reading: what each sequenced sample was, and which labels the study varied. It runs a pass of the study-reading kind, one study per unit.

seqforge pass start study-reading --ceiling-usd 2 --studies <folder>
seqforge study write-reading --out <folder>

The first command needs the gateway and the record, paper and ontology stores. It reads each study's bounds.yaml in the folder, so run it after step 1. For the standard set, add --name job-reading.yaml to the write, so the job's file sits beside the set's own five worked readings.

Each study sends at most 4 requests to Jev at once. So --units-at-once 2 keeps at most 8 Jev requests in flight.

docs.title: What the reader reads
docs.text:
The reader reads the study's bounds.yaml, and from the stores:

  • the records of the Series that the bounds keep;
  • the sequenced samples of those Series;
  • the bounds' papers: the full text where the paper store holds one, and the abstract where it does not.

Only a sequenced sample gets a row, so a microarray sample is left out. The reader never reads a supplementary file of GEO or of a paper. A label that only such a file gives is unknown.

docs.title: How the reader decides
docs.text:
Two models and code share the work.

  1. A writing model lists the options. DeepSeek Flash (deepseek/deepseek-flash), with thinking on, reads the records and the papers. It lists the factors, the labels that the study varied on purpose, with their levels and baseline. It lists every value that each label takes, each with a quote. It does not say which sample has which value. An answer that cannot be used is asked for once more.
  2. Jev answers every closed question. It says whether each factor was varied on purpose, which level is the baseline, and whether the levels are in order. Then, for each sample, it picks the sample's level on each factor and its value on each label, from the writer's lists.
  3. Some questions are asked twice. Whether a factor was varied is asked plain and negated. Its baseline, and each sample's level, are asked with the options in order and then reversed. Each sample's label values are asked once.
  4. Code finds every quote. A quote from a record must be in its named field, character for character. A quote from a paper must be in the paper once each run of spaces and line breaks is one space. Jev then judges whether each found passage backs its claim, or speaks against it. A claim is quoted only from a found passage that backs it. Otherwise it is inferred.
  5. Code writes the reading. It drops a factor level that no sample is at, copies each sample's BioSample accession, and runs the format check.

A sample's BioSample accession is the SAMN id that its GEO record links. Code copies it into the sample's row as biosample_accession, only when the record links exactly one. It is an id, not a claim. A compile joins a reading into its sample table by this id.

The writer gets no JSON schema, because the gateway cannot send DeepSeek a schema while it thinks. Code reads the JSON object out of the reply's text instead. The reply must be all JSON, or hold exactly one fenced block.

docs.title: Assay guides
docs.text:
An assay guide is a short text that the reader adds to the writer's instructions and to Jev's questions, for a study whose records name one kind of assay. One guide exists today, for pull-down assays: ChIP-seq, ChIP-exo, CUT&RUN and CUT&Tag. In these assays an antibody pulls down the chromatin bound by one protein or histone mark, and a control library measures the background.

The guide says that the target is a label and never a factor. It asks the writer to tie each control library to the pull-down libraries made from the same material, by the words that tie them, such as a replicate number in the sample titles. Jev checks each tie. Libraries that are tied share one biosample id. That biosample label is an id the reader makes up, such as B1. It is not the BioSample accession.

docs.title: Ontology ids
docs.text:
An ontology id names a term in a standard vocabulary, such as UBERON:0002107, the liver in UBERON, a vocabulary of body parts. The ids come from liulab-data's ontology store, found through LABDATA_ONTOLOGIES or the pointer that liulab-data saves. The pass opens the store once when it starts. The store keeps each vocabulary's snapshot fixed until the pass ends. If the store cannot be opened, pass start exits 2 and says why. It never reads a study with no search.

  • The species id is the record's own taxonomy id.
  • healthy is PATO:0000461, from PATO, the ontology of traits and qualities.
  • A development_stage of adult is the species' adult stage, found by its whole name. For the mouse, that is mature stage in MmusDv, the ontology of mouse life stages.
  • Every other id comes from a search of the store: up to 10 candidates, whole-text matches first. Jev picks one or none, and a term is written only when Jev's pick has a probability of 0.8 or more.

The store must name an id, or the id is not written. A vocabulary that the store does not hold finds nothing, so its labels get no id. The reading's ontology_snapshot names each snapshot that its ids came from, such as liulab-data ontology store: cl-2026-11-13, efo-3.96.0, ncbitaxon-2026-11-26, pato-2026-10-01. Its date is the day in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) when the pass opened the store, because the store names its snapshots by UTC day.

docs.title: How the reader ends a study
docs.text:
seqforge study write-reading --out <folder> writes each study's answer as <folder>/<ID>/reading.yaml, or under the name that --name gives. It follows the same rules as write-bounds: it never overwrites a file, it writes no file that fails the format check, and it refuses while a pass holds the task.

Ending When File Settled Jev's two answers agree on every question asked twice, and Jev answered every question asked once Written Unsettled Jev's two answers disagree on whether a factor was varied on purpose, on its baseline, or on a sample's level. Or Jev left a question asked once unanswered. A missing answer, or a probability of exactly 0.5, never agrees Written, with each probability Refused The writer's answer cannot be used after one retry, the store holds no sequenced sample of the study, the writer lists more than 25 values for one label, or the reading fails the format check None. write-reading prints the reason Held The key is not a GEO Series, the study's bounds file is missing or fails its check, the record store does not hold a kept Series, or the study has papers and no paper store is set None. seqforge pass status study-reading lists the study under not_done

A question asked once is one of these: a sample's value on a label, a label with no listed value, where the libraries' material came from, whether a factor's levels are in order, a passage check, a tie, or a term pick. When Jev leaves one unanswered, its claim is unknown with no probability.

docs.title: 4. Check the reading
docs.text:
seqforge study check-reading <folder>/<ID>/reading.yaml

The check reads one reading file and accepts or rejects it. It prints the same JSON object as check-bounds, with the same exit codes. It also exits 2, with no verdict, when liulab-data is not installed, because liulab-data's vocabularies judge each ontology id.

The check looks at the structure of the file:

  • every sample has every label;
  • every claim says how it is backed, in exactly one way;
  • every passage that a claim cites, for it or against it, is in the file;
  • a file that writes an ontology id names where its ids came from, and each id is from its label's vocabulary.

The check does not look for a quote in the record that the quote names. That needs the records, so it belongs to step 3.

docs.title: 5. Work out the relations
docs.text:
seqforge study relations <folder>/<ID>/reading.yaml

The command checks the file as check-reading does, and rejects it the same way. For a valid file, its JSON also holds relations. Code works the relations out from the reading's labels each time the command runs. No file stores them, so a relation is never out of date with its reading.

Relation Key Meaning Replicates replicates Samples with the same assay, the same target, the same control type and the same level of every factor. Contrasts contrasts Two groups of samples that differ in one factor, with the other factors equal. One group is at the baseline, such as untreated. Series series Samples in order along a factor whose levels have an order, such as time points or doses. This kind of series is not a GEO Series. Shared biosamples shared_biosample Samples made from the same material, such as two assays on one piece of tissue. Signal-to-control pairs signal_to_control A library that has a target, paired with its background control library made from the same material, such as an input library.

docs.title: 6. Run the chain unattended
docs.text:
seqforge study run --studies <folder> --ceiling-usd <dollars>

This command needs the gateway and all three stores. It runs four commands in order over the studies of one folder:

  1. pass start study-bounds;
  2. study write-bounds, which writes each study's bounds.yaml;
  3. pass start study-reading, which reads the bounds just written;
  4. study write-reading, which writes each study's reading.yaml.

--studies is required. With no --keys, the command runs the studies that the folder's pick.yaml lists. One --ceiling-usd covers both passes: bounding spends first, and reading gets what is left. --model, --units-at-once and --off-peak-only work as they do for pass start. A --model role goes to each pass whose kind has that role.

Each pass uses its default task, seqforge/passes/<kind>/ in the current folder. The command adds no check of its own. It always writes the folder's own bounds.yaml and reading.yaml, so it cannot write the standard set's job-bounds.yaml and job-reading.yaml. Use steps 1 and 3 with --name for those.

It prints one JSON object: the folder, the ceiling, spent_usd, and steps, with each step's command (verb), its exit code (exit) and its own output.

Exit When 0 Every step finished. 2 A setup a step cannot use. A setup refused before the first pass spends nothing. 3 A pass stopped, such as at the ceiling, a task was held by another process, or the format check rejected a file.

The first step that does not finish stops the chain, and its exit code is the command's. To resume, run the same command again from the same folder. Every study already answered replays from the gateway's cache at no cost. A file already written is kept.

Each run of the standard set is measured in a dated note under docs/research/: what it cost, how long it took and how each study ended. The latest is the note on the run of 2026-11-27.

docs.title: After the chain
docs.text:
Two commands use a study folder once the chain has written it:

  • seqforge report --study <folder>/<ID> writes report.html and report.json into that study folder. It shows the folder's own bounds.yaml and reading.yaml, never the job-*.yaml files. It does not show whether the job settled the study: that is kept in the pass's task.
  • seqforge run --study <folder>/<ID> joins the reading into the compiled sample_metadata.tsv by BioSample accession, when you compile the study's FASTQ files. From FASTQ files to a pipeline says more.

docs.title: Files that exist today
docs.text: Files from the hand work lists every bounds file, reading and verdict made so far: where each one is, its format and who made it.

docs.title: Example reports
docs.text:
Three study reports, made by seqforge from public GEO records. Each one is a single web page that opens offline. Open one before you read anything else on this site: it shows what seqforge writes about a study, and how each claim points back to its source.

The three studies come from the standard set, 50 GEO studies picked to cover many kinds of design. They were picked here because their designs differ, and because each reading quotes only public text: GEO records, and at most a paper's abstract on PubMed.

Study What it is Design the reading found Quotes from Job's ending GSE112068 Human lung cells exposed to a drug that damages DNA, sampled over 8 days 3 factors: treatment, dose and time point (11 times). 23 samples GEO records only Settled GSE272899 Open chromatin in fat-tissue immune cells of young and old mice 2 factors: age and genotype (4 genotypes). 9 samples GEO records and one abstract Settled GSE329430 Bone marrow and brain cells in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease 4 factors: genotype, disease, tissue and cell type. 20 samples GEO records and one abstract Unsettled

docs.title: How to read a report
docs.text:
A report has one tab, Study, in three parts.

  • Bounds. Which GEO Series and papers are one study. A solid box is a record kept in the study, and a dashed, struck-through box is one left out. Point at a record to see why it was kept or left out.
  • Design. The factors the study varied on purpose, and how many samples fall in each mix of levels. A diamond (◆) marks a factor's baseline, the level the others are compared with. Each factor carries a p: the model's confidence in that factor, from 0 to 1. Point at a count to list its samples.
  • Samples. What each sample was, in one table per topic: assay, organism, material, and treatment and time. Each value is either quoted (a passage backs it), inferred (no passage states it), unknown or n/a (it does not apply). A paler cell has a lower p. Click a cell to see the passages behind it, each with the record and field it came from.

A report does not show how the job ended the study. The table above says it, and so does each section below.

docs.title: GSE112068: a dose and time course
docs.text:
Human IMR-90 cells, a line of lung fibroblasts taken from a fetus at 16 weeks, were treated with bleomycin, a drug that breaks DNA. The reading found three factors: treatment (none or bleomycin), dose (0, 2 or 40 µg/ml) and time point (11 times, from the start to 8 days). Each factor has a baseline, and the levels of all three run in order. The study has no paper, so every quote comes from the GEO Series and Sample records.

Both jobs settled it: each question asked twice got the same answer both times.

Open the GSE112068 report.

docs.title: GSE272899: two factors, and a chromatin assay
docs.text:
ATAC-seq (a method that maps the open, readable parts of the genome) of macrophages sorted from mouse fat tissue. The mice were young or old, and carried one of four genotypes around the gene GDF3, among them a knockout in myeloid cells, the blood-cell family that macrophages belong to. Every mouse got the same dose of LPS, a bacterial toxin, for 4 hours. The reading records that dose as a shared label and not as a factor, since all samples got it. Quotes come from the GEO records and the paper's PubMed abstract.

Both jobs settled it.

Open the GSE272899 report.

docs.title: GSE329430: four factors, left unsettled
docs.text:
Bone marrow and brain cells from 12-month-old female mice, some carrying 5xFAD, a model of Alzheimer's disease. The reading found four factors: genotype, disease, tissue and cell type. Some of the 20 samples are not RNA at all. They are tag libraries read beside the RNA, which mark each cell's mouse or its surface proteins, and the reading lists them as assays of their own: CMO and HTO (tags that mark which mouse a cell came from) and ADT (antibody tags that count surface proteins). Quotes come from the GEO records and the paper's PubMed abstract.

The reading job left it unsettled. Each question is asked twice, the second time with the options in reverse order. Here the two answers differed on two points: whether treatment was varied on purpose, and which cell type is the baseline. The file and the report still show the first answer, so treat those two points as open.

Open the GSE329430 report.

docs.title: How these were made
docs.text:
All three were made on 2026-11-27, from a run over the whole standard set, with:

  • seqforge at commit 9209509, report version 2026.11.8;
  • the bounding job, version 2026.11.3, and the reading job, version 2026.11.10;
  • Jev 1.14.0 from TypeSafe, a model that answers yes-or-no and choice questions with a probability, in both jobs, and DeepSeek Flash as the reading job's writer;
  • ontology terms from the dated snapshots each reading names in its ontology_snapshot field.

The run cost nothing, because every answer was already in the model gateway's cache. The dated note on that run gives what a first run costs and how each of the 50 ended.

docs.title: Make one yourself
docs.text:
seqforge study run --studies <folder> --ceiling-usd 1
seqforge report --study <folder>/<GSE id>

The first command needs the lab's model gateway and its copy of the GEO and SRA records. Read your own studies says how to set up the folder and what each step needs. The second command needs neither the gateway nor the records: it reads the two files the first one wrote, and writes report.html and report.json beside them. With the lab's ontology store set up, it also names each assay term.

docs.title: The bounds file
docs.text:
A study is one piece of research: the experiments that one paper reports, or one project that has no paper yet. Public archives do not store studies. GEO, the Gene Expression Omnibus, stores Series: a Series is one deposit of samples. A Series links to papers and to other Series, and not everything it links to belongs to the same study.

A study's bounds say what belongs to it: which GEO Series, and which papers. The bounds file writes the bounds down, one file per study, in YAML, a plain-text format of fields and lists. Every later step reads it. The reading file is drawn only from the Series and the papers that the bounds keep.

This page describes every field and every rule of the file. It is all you need to read one.

docs.title: A short example
docs.text:
This is the bounds file that the bounding job wrote for the standard-set study GSE131269. The job kept the Series and one paper, and it left a second linked paper out.

format: 1
study: GSE131269
models:
  bounds: typesafe/jev-1.14.0
  probabilities: typesafe/jev-1.14.0
series:
- id: GSE131269
  inferred: 'code: the study starts from GSE131269'
  p: null
papers:
- pmid:32494643
left_out:
- id: pmid:31279658
  inferred: 'Jev''s p(yes) that pmid:31279658 first reports the data of GEO Series GSE131269: 0.10; its
    p(yes) to the reversed question: 0.89'
  p: 0.9
reason: Code kept GEO Series GSE131269; Jev judged each other record kept here to be from the same research.
passages: {}
titles:
  GSE131269: Identification of the m6Am Methyltransferase PCIF1 Reveals the Location and Functions of
    m6Am in the Transcriptome.
  pmid:31279658: Identification of the m6Am Methyltransferase PCIF1 Reveals the Location and Functions
    of m6Am in the Transcriptome.
  pmid:32494643: N6-adenosine methylation of ribosomal RNA affects lipid oxidation and stress resistance.

Read it from the top:

  • series keeps one Series. Code kept it because the study starts from it.
  • papers keeps one paper, by its PubMed id (PMID).
  • left_out holds the other linked paper. Jev, a model that answers yes-or-no questions with a probability, judged that this paper does not first report the study's data. Its p of 0.9 is the chance that this judgement is right.
  • titles gives each record's title, so you can read the file without opening GEO or PubMed.

docs.title: Where the files are
docs.text:
File What it is <folder>/<ID>/bounds.yaml A study's bounds. seqforge study write-bounds --out <folder> writes one per study from the bounding pass's answers. seqforge study run runs that pass and that write as its first two steps, and calls models through the model gateway. evals/standard-set/<ID>/bounds.yaml The bounds of each of the 50 studies of the standard set. evals/standard-set/<ID>/job-bounds.yaml The bounds that the bounding job drew for each of the same 50 studies, written with study write-bounds --name job-bounds.yaml.

<ID> is the study's name, such as GSE131269. study write-bounds never overwrites a file that is already there. It writes no file for a study that the job refused, and it writes no text that the format check rejects.

To check one file, run:

seqforge study check-bounds evals/standard-set/GSE101112/bounds.yaml

The check reads the file alone. It needs no model and no network. See The check.

docs.title: The fields
docs.text:
Every field below is required, except titles. The check rejects a file with any other field.

Field Holds format The whole number 1. See When the format changes. study The study's name: the GEO Series it was picked by, such as GSE101112. It cannot be empty. models Who wrote the file. bounds is the model that drew the bounds. probabilities is the model that gave the p values. Either may be null. series The Series that belong to the study. At least one. Each entry is a claim, and its id is written GSE<number>. papers The papers that report the study, each written pmid:<number>. The list may be empty. left_out Each linked Series or paper that does not belong. Each entry is a claim. The list may be empty. reason One line that says why these Series and papers are one study. It cannot be blank. passages The quotes that back the claims, each under its number. It may be empty: {}. See Passages. titles Optional. The title of each record that the file places, under the record's id. See Titles.

docs.title: What belongs, and how a record is placed
docs.text:
A study is whole Series. A Series is in the study or it is left out. No field names some of a Series' samples. Telling apart the experiments inside one Series is the job of a later step, not of the bounds.

A SuperSeries is left out. A SuperSeries is a GEO Series that groups other Series, its sub-Series. For a study that starts from a SuperSeries, series lists the sub-Series, and the SuperSeries itself goes in left_out. So the study's name is not always one of its series.

A record is placed once. Each Series or paper is in series, in papers or in left_out. It is never in two of them, and never twice in one. A left-out record's id may be a Series or a paper, and it cannot be blank.

docs.title: Claims
docs.text:
A claim is one decision that the file makes: one Series kept, or one record left out. Each entry of series and of left_out is a claim. A kept paper is not a claim: it is a plain pmid: entry under papers.

A claim holds the record's id, exactly one backing mark, and p. A backing mark says how the claim is backed.

Field Holds id The record: a Series such as GSE101112, or a paper such as pmid:33294943. It cannot be blank. quoted Backing mark. A source says it. The mark lists the numbers of the passages that say so. inferred Backing mark. No passage says it outright. The mark is a short text that says how it was worked out. unknown Backing mark. What was read does not say. The mark is a short note. see Optional, and never beside quoted. The numbers of the passages that the claim rests on. p A number from 0 to 1, or null. Required.

The rules for a claim:

  • It has exactly one of quoted, inferred and unknown. The check rejects a claim with none, and a claim with two.
  • quoted lists at least one passage.
  • Every number in quoted and in see must be a passage in the file.
  • The text after inferred or unknown cannot be blank.

In left_out, the backing mark is also the reason that the record does not belong. For an inferred claim, the reason is its text. For a quoted claim, the reason is what its passages say. There is no separate reason field.
